items.title: Verstappen wins chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole
items.why: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix by 0.639 seconds from McLaren's Lando Norris, with Oscar Piastri third. New champion Kimi Antonelli lost two places on the final lap to finish fourth. Ferrari team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided again.
items.matters: It was Verstappen's 75th career win and lifts him to second in the drivers' standings.
items.changed: Updated: the race has been run and Verstappen won

items.title: Indonesia factory fire kills three; 36 workers missing
items.why: A fire at a sweets factory in Serang, in Indonesia's Banten province west of Jakarta, killed at least three people on Saturday, officials say. Rescuers are searching for 36 missing workers; 15 people were rescued alive. Survivors say it started at a cooling unit; the cause is under investigation.

items.title: South Korea's education minister resigns over AI exam cheating fears
items.why: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, and President Lee Jae Myung accepted. He took responsibility for last-minute rules to stop AI-assisted cheating in Thursday's Suneung university entrance exam. Officials say 111 test-takers were caught with smart devices.
items.matters: It began when a top scorer in a national accountancy exam admitted using a hidden camera and phone.

items.title: India post record 720-9 in first Test against New Zealand
items.why: India declared on 720 for nine at the Basin Reserve in Wellington, New Zealand, the highest Test total ever made in the country. KL Rahul scored 136 and Rishabh Pant 128. New Zealand closed day four on 119 for two, 233 runs behind.

items.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack sparks fire; tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz
items.why: Bahrain says it intercepted several Iranian missile and drone attacks late on Saturday, and one hit a civilian industrial site, causing a fire but no injuries. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they targeted US radars at bases in Bahrain. At least three tankers were also struck in or near the strait.
items.matters: The strait carries a large share of the world's oil, so attacks there affect energy prices everywhere.

items.title: England beat New Zealand 37-12 for record win over All Blacks
items.why: England scored five tries to beat New Zealand 37-12 at Twickenham in London on Saturday in the Nations Championship. The 25-point margin is England's largest against the All Blacks and New Zealand's heaviest defeat in the northern hemisphere.

items.title: Alcaraz fights back to beat Shelton and reach ATP Finals final
items.why: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz beat Ben Shelton of the US 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 in the first semi-final of the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, on Saturday. He meets Germany's Alexander Zverev in Sunday's final.

items.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal after ten years of talks
items.why: The European Union and Indonesia signed a trade agreement and an investment protection deal in Brussels on Saturday. Indonesia says 90.4% of its goods will enter the EU duty-free. The EU gains easier access to a market of 280 million people and to nickel for batteries.
items.matters: Both sides still need to ratify it; Indonesia expects it to take effect in 2027.

items.title: Brazil's former president Bolsonaro in intensive care with bowel blockage
items.why: Jair Bolsonaro, 71, is in intensive care at a hospital in Brazil's capital, Brasília, with an intestinal obstruction, the hospital said on Saturday. It says he is stable and conscious. He is serving a 27-year sentence for a coup plot under house arrest; he denies the charges.

items.title: Mexico captures FBI-wanted cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro' in Sinaloa
items.why: Mexican forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, an alleged Beltrán Leyva cartel leader on the FBI's ten most wanted list, in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday night. Mexico's military says seven gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the firefight. Roadblocks were later set up across the state.
items.matters: He faces charges in Mexico and the US, where a $5m reward had been offered for him.

items.title: Swimmer braves Strait of Hormuz to highlight war's harm to wildlife
items.why: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh, a UN Patron of the Oceans, swam about 15km in stages over three days from Oman's Musandam Peninsula around the Cape of Hormuz. He says he saw tankers hit nearby. He warns pollution could harm coral reefs, mangroves, turtles and dolphins.

items.title: EU budget plan proposes a 3% tax on big tech companies
items.why: European Council President António Costa on Saturday proposed a 2028–2034 EU budget €204bn smaller than the Commission's plan. It includes a 3% levy on large firms' EU revenue from online advertising, digital services and user data, plus taxes on e-waste and tobacco. Several governments have criticised it.
items.matters: Tax changes need every EU country to agree, and the levy could anger the US government.

items.title: Drones set Russian cargo ship on fire in Gulf of Finland
items.why: Russian officials say two drones hit the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship Sparta II on Saturday; it caught fire in Finnish waters. The crew was evacuated to another ship. Finland's armed forces say Ukraine was likely behind it; Ukraine has not commented. Finland also says a Russian helicopter briefly entered its airspace.
items.matters: Finland's prime minister, Petteri Orpo, said 'war is spilling over into our immediate vicinity'.
items.changed: Updated: crew evacuated; Finland says Ukraine likely behind it and reports a Russian airspace breach

items.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa's first woman deputy president, dies at 71
items.why: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka died on Friday evening of complications from a medical procedure about two weeks earlier, her family said. She was South Africa's deputy president from 2005 to 2008 and led UN Women from 2013 to 2021.
items.matters: President Cyril Ramaphosa and UN chief António Guterres led tributes to a long-time campaigner for women's rights.

items.title: Russian missile strike on Zelensky's hometown kills two, wounds 60
items.why: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine on Friday night. Local officials say a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed and 60 people were wounded, including six children. About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools were damaged, the city's head says.

items.title: Cricket Australia gives Pat Cummins unanimous backing as Test captain
items.why: Cricket Australia's board says Pat Cummins keeps its 'unanimous support' as captain, after former teammates Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft said the 2018 ball-tampering plot was widely known. Cummins denies knowing. The board ruled out a new inquiry but set up a forum for players to share accounts.
items.matters: Separately, Fox Cricket says Khawaja and David Warner will be 'rested' from its commentary for the coming weeks.

items.title: Nations agree to work on rules for AI 'killer robots' by 2028
items.why: At UN-backed talks in Geneva, the 128 states in the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons agreed early on Saturday to 'elaborate' an instrument on lethal autonomous weapons over two years. Nearly 100 countries wanted binding rules sooner; campaigners say the US and Russia blocked stronger wording.
items.matters: Weapons that choose and attack targets without a human decision are already being developed and tested.

items.title: Magnitude 6.7 earthquake shakes central Peru; no injuries reported
items.why: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck central Peru's Junín region on Friday evening, about 129km deep, Peru's Geophysical Institute says. Civil defence officials reported landslides on roads, damaged homes and a hospital, and power cuts, but no injuries. Shaking was felt in the capital, Lima.
items.matters: Peru sits on one of the world's most active earthquake zones; deep quakes like this can be felt hundreds of kilometres away.

items.title: US media report hacks at FBI crime database and farm agency
items.why: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, used by police across the US, NBC News and CNN reported on Friday. Separately, a US Department of Agriculture system for paying farmers was hit by a cyberattack, officials said. It is unclear who is responsible.
items.matters: The FBI database holds warrant and background-check records used by police every day.

items.title: US jury convicts man of starting deadly 2025 Palisades Fire
items.why: A federal jury in Los Angeles convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of starting the blaze that became the January 2025 Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people. His first trial ended without a verdict in June. He faces five to 40 years in prison, prosecutors say.
items.matters: The fire destroyed more than 6,800 buildings in Los Angeles and Malibu, Cal Fire says.

items.title: Child dies of measles in Virginia, first such death since 1978
items.why: The Virginia Department of Health says a child aged under five who tested positive for measles has died. Officials say it is the state's first measles death since 1978. Virginia has 220 cases this year; US states have reported 12 measles deaths in 2026.
items.matters: Health officials say two doses of the MMR vaccine give about 97% protection.

items.title: Bolivian university holds guinea pig festival with races and fashion show
items.why: Students at the Public University of El Alto, next to Bolivia's seat of government La Paz, held their second guinea pig festival on Friday. Guinea pigs raced, boxed, were weighed and paraded in costumes; the heaviest weighed 2.5 kilograms. A symbolic guinea pig wedding closed the event.
items.matters: Organisers want to revive the Andean animal, domesticated there thousands of years ago, in Bolivian diets and rituals.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches after 13-year wait to record sales
items.why: Rockstar Games says the video game took about $3.79bn in retail sales in its first day after going on sale on Thursday, nearly five times Grand Theft Auto V's first day in 2013. Reviews have been glowing: its Metacritic score is 99 out of 100.
items.matters: Rockstar calls it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history; the game cost more than $1bn to make.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 for first time since July
items.why: The cryptocurrency bitcoin dropped below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, Reuters reported, as a sell-off in AI-linked shares spread to riskier assets. Bloomberg put it 5.1% lower at about $58,333 late on Friday.

items.title: Nvidia shares tumble after report of US regulator accounting inquiry
items.why: Shares in US chipmaker Nvidia fell about 14% on Friday, CNBC reports, after Reuters said Securities and Exchange Commission staff were examining possible accounting issues. The SEC declined to comment; an inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. Nvidia has had seven straight weekly losses.
items.matters: Nvidia's chips power much of the AI industry, so its troubles affect the wider stock market.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims proof of Riemann hypothesis using Claude AI
items.why: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic, said on Friday that, working with its Claude model, he had found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a problem about prime numbers open since 1859. He released it only in Lean, a language computers use to check proofs.
items.matters: It is a $1m Millennium Prize problem; mathematicians say checking the proof and explaining it to humans will take time.

items.title: US court jails Indian man over plot to kill Sikh separatist
items.why: A federal judge in New York sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months, more than 19 years, on Friday for plotting to have Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun killed. US prosecutors say an Indian intelligence officer directed the plot; India denies any involvement.
items.matters: The case has strained relations between the United States and India, and between India and Canada.

items.title: Estonia to close all road crossings with Russia from 1 December
items.why: Estonia's government decided on Friday to shut its five road checkpoints with Russia for six months from 1 December, citing hostile Russian activity; rail freight will continue. Russia's foreign ministry accused Estonia of trying to "erect a new Iron Curtain".
items.matters: About 760,000 crossings were made this year; Finland has kept its border with Russia closed since 2023.

items.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
items.why: Denmark ordered Russia's defence attaché to leave within seven days on Friday. Its intelligence service says Russian intelligence planned to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner at a September concert near Copenhagen; two Danish men are charged. Russia's embassy called the move "vengeful" and says no evidence was shown.
items.matters: Danish intelligence says it is the first Russian assassination attempt of its kind in Denmark.

items.title: EU and UK agree post-Brexit reset on youth mobility and trade
items.why: At a summit in Brussels on Friday, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and EU leaders agreed a youth scheme letting up to 100,000 young people from each side live and work in the other for up to three years, plus deals on food standards and linking carbon markets.
items.matters: EU officials say the deal depends on Britain agreeing lower university fees for EU students within six months.

items.title: 57th International Film Festival of India opens in Goa
items.why: The 57th International Film Festival of India opened on Friday in Panaji, Goa, and runs until 28 November. It is showing 159 international films from 86 countries, chosen from about 1,400 entries, opening with Polish director Paweł Pawlikowski's Cannes prize-winner Fatherland.
items.matters: Its theme is 'Stories Without Borders', with Russia as partner country and Spain as country of honour.

items.title: Poland says Russian missiles crashed on its soil near European drills
items.why: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell on its territory on Friday during an attack on Ukraine, near Nowy Lipowiec, about 60km from the Ukrainian border. Nobody was hurt. In Warsaw on Saturday, NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance 'will defend every inch of Polish territory'.
items.matters: NATO's North Atlantic Council meets on Monday to discuss the incident, which Poland calls a deliberate provocation.
items.changed: Updated: NATO's chief pledged to defend Poland; NATO ambassadors meet in Brussels on Monday

items.title: Spain to face France in Nations League quarter-finals
items.why: Friday's draw in Nyon, Switzerland, also paired England with Norway, Portugal with the Netherlands and Belgium with Germany. The two-legged ties will be played between 25 and 30 March, and the finals tournament on 9 to 13 June, at a venue not yet chosen.

items.title: Myanmar rejects UN court ruling that it committed genocide against Rohingya
items.why: Myanmar's military government on Friday called "unfair" the International Court of Justice's ruling that its forces committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims in 2017. The court, in The Hague, ordered compensation and safe return for those displaced; it was the first time it found a state responsible for genocide.
items.matters: About 1.2 million Rohingya live in camps in Bangladesh; the court has very limited means of enforcing its rulings.

items.title: Iraqi forces enter Kataib Hezbollah stronghold after oil smuggling dispute
items.why: Iraqi troops and police deployed on Friday in Jurf al-Sakhar, in Babil province south of Baghdad, under a deal for the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah to leave. The government accuses the group of smuggling state oil worth hundreds of millions of dollars; it denies this.
items.matters: The US has pressed Iraq to disarm Iran-aligned militias, some of which have attacked US forces this year.

items.title: Young people protest over living costs in more than 25 European countries
items.why: Students and workers rallied across Europe on Friday: in Italy the CGIL union held a general strike with protests in more than 100 places, and there were marches in Germany, Austria, Croatia, Spain and Britain. They want better wages, cheaper housing and more spending on education rather than defence.
items.matters: Police in Vienna used pepper spray and made arrests; more protests are planned this weekend, including in France.

items.title: Russian barrage damages three Kyiv bridges; at least nine killed in Ukraine
items.why: Russian missiles and drones hit three bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv overnight into Friday. Kyiv's mayor says seven people died in the capital and 17 were injured; Ukrainian officials put the national toll at at least nine. Russia says it targeted bridges used for military supplies.
items.matters: France has asked for an urgent UN Security Council meeting; as of Saturday morning no date had been announced.
items.changed: Updated: officials say at least nine were killed, seven in Kyiv; no date yet for a UN Security Council meeting

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says it shot down Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh
items.why: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh early on Saturday; AFP and Reuters journalists in the city reported explosions. It followed coalition strikes on Friday on the port of Hodeidah and sites in Sanaa. No casualties were reported.
items.matters: Houthi forces are also pressing towards Aden, the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government.
items.changed: Updated: the coalition says it intercepted three more missiles fired at Riyadh early on Saturday
Updated: the final text drops named fossil fuel language; approval session under way on Sunday
items.title: COP31 climate talks run into second day of overtime over fossil fuels
items.why: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, was due to end on Friday. A final text released on Sunday drops any named mention of fossil fuels, pointing instead to a 2023 pledge to move away from them. It targets electricity making up 35% of energy use by 2035.
items.matters: The talks decide how fast countries move away from fossil fuels and how much help poorer nations get to adapt.
